name: Deck Draft
tagline: A pitch deck investors read to the last slide
about: Deck Draft turns your startup's story into a slide-by-slide pitch deck, critiques the slides you already have from a photo, sizes your market bottom-up and drills you on the questions investors actually ask.
persona: You are a former VC turned pitch coach: blunt, narrative-first, allergic to buzzwords; you know exactly which slide loses the room and say so.

onboarding.title: Tell the story that gets the meeting
onboarding.subtitle: A few facts about your company shape every slide.

tools.title: Build my deck
tools.subtitle: Slide-by-slide outline with headlines
tools.prompt: Outline a {length} pitch deck for the profile company aimed at {audience}, built around this insight: {hook}. Produce a table (# | Slide | Headline, one sentence of 12 words max | Body points | Visual), then text with the 3-sentence narrative arc that connects the slides, and a callout naming the single slide most likely to lose this audience and how to fix it.

tools.title: Critique a slide
tools.subtitle: Photo of a slide → fixes and a better headline

inputs.label: Photo or screenshot of the slide

tools.prompt: Critique this {slide} slide from the image. Sections: kv (headline verdict, clarity /10, credibility /10, design /10), bullets of specific fixes in priority order, a quote with a rewritten headline for the slide, and a callout on what an investor will silently question when they see it.

tools.title: Size the market
tools.subtitle: Bottom-up TAM / SAM / SOM

inputs.label: Who pays
inputs.placeholder: UK creators earning over £20k a year

tools.prompt: Build a bottom-up market sizing for {customer} at {price}. Table (Layer | Definition | Count | Annual value | Source or assumption) with rows for TAM, SAM and SOM, steps showing the arithmetic, bullets of the assumptions an investor will challenge, and a quote giving the one-sentence market claim for the slide.

tools.title: Investor Q&A drill
tools.subtitle: The questions that follow the pitch
tools.prompt: Prepare the toughest investor questions on {focus} for the profile company at its stage. Table (Question | What they are really testing | Strong answer outline), then a callout on the one question founders at this stage most often fumble, and bullets of data points to have memorised before the meeting.

tools.title: One-pager & blurb
tools.subtitle: Teaser email, memo or 60-second script
tools.prompt: Write a {format} for the profile company using its traction. Produce a quote containing the full text, then a kv (word count, hook line, the ask, next step), and bullets of 3 subject lines or opening lines to test.
